newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to see trade deficit in 1997 - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to see trade deficit in 1997 - analysts.

text.p: Mexico's growing imports will outstrip exports and lead to trade deficits during the second half of this year, analysts said on Tuesday.
Sergio Martin, research director at ING-Barings in Mexico City, forecast Mexico would post a trade surplus of $79 million in July, and then a deficit of $39 million in August.
"There are two factors. On the one hand, the economic recovery that has been under way, and on the other, the current (peso-dollar) exchange rate," he said.

ING-Barings forecast Mexican exports would total $106.7 billion in 1997, marginally ahead of an expected $105.3 billion in imports, to close the year with an estimated surplus of about $1.4 billlion. This compares with a surplus of $6.292 billion posted in 1996.
Hector Chavez, deputy economic research director at Santander Investment in Mexico City, also estimated Mexico would post a trade deficit during the second half of the year.
Chavez forecast Mexico would chalk up a trade surplus of $850 million for the second quarter of the year, down from 1.347 for the first quarter.
"After that, we expect a deficit or to end flat," he said. "Exports, instead of going abroad, are beginning to flow into the domestic market, and then imports are growing."
